passages.note: Final passage (concurrence in Senate amendments) of a single-subject tenancy bill, 48-26, so not near-unanimous; the Assembly floor roll call itself shows he held this office in 2019.
passages.actor_quote: Reyes, Luz Rivas, Robert Rivas, Rodriguez

passages.provision_quote: Subject to subdivision (b), an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase.
passages.note: Bill-text page for the same record: it prints the operative rent cap and just-cause sections but names no voter, so actor and tally are null here.

rows.reasoning: Rivas voted Aye on final passage of AB 1482 (2019-2020), a single-subject tenancy bill whose operative sections cap annual rent increases at "5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower" and bar termination "without just cause" on units that previously had no such protection, which is "Strengthen existing rent stabilization and extend coverage to more units". It does not "cover all rental units communitywide": the act exempts "Housing that has been issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years" and lets an owner "establish the initial rental rate" for a new tenancy. Because it adds protections rather than keeping the status quo, it also excludes "Maintain current tenant protections while allowing market rents for new construction".
